newsitem.title: UK: LME VOLATILE IN LATE TRADE, MARKETS END UNCERTAIN.
newsitem.headline: LME VOLATILE IN LATE TRADE, MARKETS END UNCERTAIN.

text.p: Late trading on the LME on Tuesday was volatile, with copper and aluminium witnessing savage late movements prior to a mostly lower close for the complex.
At one stage it appeared as if prices were about to go into free fall as fund sales and dealer liquidation battered prices to late-afternoon lows, traders said.
But copper and aluminium in particular found some late buying, with the red metal actually ending modestly higher. Other metals, however, remained depressed and closed sharply lower.
"What happened this afternoon was that a lot of people who bought the dip at midday found there wasn't a bounce and just liquidated," one trader said.
Zinc highlighted the day's trend, falling steeply after a 1,400-tonne stock increase that gave credence to talk of Chinese shipments of some 20,000 tonnes of metal to Singapore.
Also, the spread backwardations eased considerably throughout the sessions, with cash/threes at $115/125 by the close against levels of $155/165 on Monday.
Prices were pulled under $1,500, and now look set for further chart-based losses. Last business was at $1,480 a tonne, down $63 from Monday's kerb.
Copper appeared to be set to conclusively break out of the $2,260/70 to $2,320/30 band, but failed to trigger the expected sell-stops in the mid-$2,250s.
This averted the possibility of a sell-off to $2,220/30, and induced a late covering rally. Three months ended at $2,278, up $4.
The market was also helped by dry weather affecting shipments of concentrate from the OK Tedi mine in papua New Guinea again.
Aluminium cascaded below $1,700 briefly, but was buttressed by chart-based support, and with copper rallying managed to close at $1,715.
However, this was still $35 down from Monday, and with a surprising stock increase of 725 tonnes taking place the market looks vulnerable. The backwardation was also moderately narrower.
Nickel fell to fresh intra-day lows during the kerb, but remained volatile with the market seen as oversold in the short-term.
There were bouts of short-covering earlier, and similar buying in coming sessions will make for jumpy trade. Last business was at $6,700, down $160.
Lead dropped to a fresh 22-month low of $596 today, but the pace of trading was slower than in the other metals and the decline was somewhat muted. Three months finished at $598, down $8.
Tin was battered by a combination of trade and Chinese selling as well as liquidation sales, and dropped under $5,400 briefly before concluding at $5,415, down $95 from Monday.
Alloy was indicated at a softer $1,515/25 at the close.
